title: Code Reviewer Worker API, version 1
description: The Worker contract (#316, #318): what a Worker may do with the per-job credential and nothing more. The app serves GET /api/workers/v1/jobs/{id}, POST /api/workers/v1/jobs/{id}/heartbeat and POST /api/workers/v1/jobs/{id}/result. Every request carries 'Authorization: Bearer <credential>' (WorkerCredential in runner-api.v1.json), which is valid only for the job in the path and only while the claim that minted it holds; the dispatcher credential (RUNNER_TOKEN) is refused here and the job credential is refused by the runner API. The Worker never sees the dispatcher credential and cannot claim another job. A reader ignores fields it does not know (an additive field is not a new version), except in RunnerJobInput, which stays closed: the Worker refuses unknown job fields. The App sends an optional job field only to a Worker that names the matching feature in the details request (`?features=dynamic_capabilities`, a comma separated list, unknown names ignored). #424: the details call also names the providers the Worker can run, `?llmProviders=openrouter` (a comma separated list of slugs, see WorkerJobDetailsRequest); absent means `openrouter`, and a previous-release app ignores the parameter. The app sends a provider only to a Worker that listed it. Errors have the shape and the codes of the runner API (ErrorResponse, ApiErrorCode): 401 WORKER_CREDENTIAL_INVALID (also the fourth details call of a claim: its three calls are spent, the Worker stops), 404 RUNNER_JOB_NOT_FOUND, 409 RUNNER_LEASE_LOST (stop at once), 409 RUNNER_JOB_ENDED (the app ended the job), 409 RUNNER_RESULT_CONFLICT (another result is already stored), 413 RUNNER_BODY_TOO_LARGE, 503 RUNNER_GIT_ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE with Retry-After (the job was given back; the Worker exits). The details call is allowed at most three times per claim, and each call mints a fresh installation token. Secrets (git.token, llm.apiKey) appear only in the details answer. This file is the only source of the format: the app (app/integration-tests/compatibility), the runner (runner/tests/contract) and the Dispatcher project check the examples in contracts/examples/worker-api against it.

WorkerJobDetailsRequest.description: #424: the query string of GET /api/workers/v1/jobs/{id}, as an object of its parameters. Both are optional comma separated lists: `features` (the names of KnownClaimFeature, unknown names are ignored) and `llmProviders` (slugs of LlmProviderId: the LLM providers the Worker can run; absent means `openrouter`). The app ignores the list today (the claim issue of epic #420 will use it); it still always sends `openrouter`.

WorkerJobDetailsResponse.description: 200 from GET /api/workers/v1/jobs/{id}: the job, with the git token and the model key minted at this call. Cache-Control is always no-store. The credential is not repeated here and there is no lease token: the credential is the proof of the claim.

heartbeatIntervalSeconds.description: How often to send a heartbeat; the lease is several times longer.

tokenExpiresAt.description: When the git token stops working; null if it does not expire.

WorkerHeartbeatRequest.description: The body of POST /api/workers/v1/jobs/{id}/heartbeat: empty (the credential identifies the job). A body is accepted and ignored.

WorkerHeartbeatResponse.description: 200 from the heartbeat: the lease is extended. 409 RUNNER_LEASE_LOST means the lease is lost: stop and deliver nothing.

superseded.description: #396: true when a newer push replaced this run; see HeartbeatResponse in runner-api.v1.json. Sent only to a Worker that named the feature `supersede` in its details request.

WorkerStepsRequest.description: #745: the body of POST /api/workers/v1/jobs/{id}/steps: a batch of the records of the running turn of the Implementer (the live view), at most 50 in at most 48 KiB. The credential identifies the job and proves the claim, so the body holds no lease token. The same rules and answers as POST /api/runners/v1/jobs/{id}/steps (`StepsRequest` in runner-api.v1.json): the call does NOT extend the lease, 409 RUNNER_LEASE_LOST for a lost claim, 409 RUNNER_JOB_ENDED when the job is over, 400 RUNNER_REQUEST_INVALID for a job that is not a turn of the Implementer or a record that does not fit.

WorkerStepsResponse.description: #745: 200 from the Worker's steps call: `StepsResponse` of runner-api.v1.json.

SessionPartQuery.description: #839: the query string of PUT /api/workers/v1/jobs/{id}/session, as an object of its parameters (every value is decimal digits or text in the URL). One request carries one PART of the session snapshot of a running turn of the Implementer (follow-up turns): the engine's export as the runner made it (JSON, secrets taken out, gzipped), at most 8 MiB gzipped. A function of the platform takes no request body over 4.5 MB, so the file is cut into parts of exactly 3 MiB (`bytes` / 3145728, rounded up, at most 3) and the last part is whatever is left; the body of the request is the bytes of the part (`application/octet-stream`), read up to 3 MiB (413 RUNNER_BODY_TOO_LARGE above) and exactly as long as `bytes` says for that part (400 otherwise). Every part carries the description of the whole file: `parts` (the count, which must be what `bytes` makes), `part` (this part's index from 0), `bytes` (the size of the gzip file), `rawBytes` (the size of the JSON inside it), `sha256` (the lower case hex digest of the gzip file) and `opencodeVersion` (the engine that wrote it). A part is judged on its own and may arrive in any order or twice. The app keeps the parts of the job apart; when the last one is in it puts them together, checks size and digest, and swaps the snapshot in for the session's old one (one snapshot for each session, replaced by each turn, kept for good; the old one stays readable until then). 400 RUNNER_REQUEST_INVALID names the wrong fields (`fields`), also `body` for parts that do not make the announced file or disagree with each other (nothing of that upload is kept). The call proves the claim and nothing more: it does NOT extend the lease. 409 RUNNER_JOB_ENDED when the job is over, 401 WORKER_CREDENTIAL_INVALID for a credential that is not the job's, 400 for a job that is not a turn of the Implementer. The sender is best effort: a snapshot that is not stored means the next turn starts from a summary.

SessionPartResponse.description: #839: 200 from the snapshot call. `part` and `parts` repeat the request's; `complete` is true once the whole snapshot is stored, also for a part sent again after that. Repeating a part answers 200.

ResumeSessionQuery.description: #840: the query string of GET /api/workers/v1/jobs/{id}/resume-session, as an object of its parameters. The Worker of a follow-up turn (`implementer.resume.snapshot` true) fetches the session snapshot the app stored for the job's own session (the file `PUT .../session` delivered, replaced by each turn): the engine's export, gzipped, at most 8 MiB. A response body is held to 4.5 MB like a request body, so the file comes in the same parts of exactly 3 MiB (`bytes` / 3145728, rounded up, at most 3; the last part is whatever is left) and `part` (from 0, default 0) names the one to send. 200 `application/octet-stream`: the bytes of that part, with the description of the whole file in the headers `ResumeSessionHeaders` (every part carries it, so a part is judged on its own and the parts may be fetched in any order and twice). 204 without a body: the session has no stored snapshot (never saved, or not by a turn that could). 400 RUNNER_REQUEST_INVALID (`fields`: `part`) for a part that is not a number or beyond the last. 401 WORKER_CREDENTIAL_INVALID, 409 RUNNER_JOB_ENDED / RUNNER_LEASE_LOST as for every Worker call, and 400 for a job that is not a turn of the Implementer. The call reads a snapshot of the job's own session and of no other: the app finds the session from the job. It proves the claim and nothing more: it does NOT extend the lease. The Worker checks the size and the sha256 of the whole file; a file it cannot fetch or read means the turn continues from a summary (`ImplementerResumeResult`), never a failed turn. The file holds what the earlier turns read and said, secrets of the turn taken out, tool outputs included (see the session snapshot in docs/implementer.md).

ResumeSessionHeaders.description: #840: the response headers of a 200 from GET /api/workers/v1/jobs/{id}/resume-session, as an object of lower-case header names (every value is text in the header). They describe the WHOLE file, not the part: `x-snapshot-parts` (how many parts, 1 to 3, which is what `x-snapshot-bytes` makes), `x-snapshot-bytes` (the size of the gzip file), `x-snapshot-raw-bytes` (the size of the JSON inside it), `x-snapshot-sha256` (the lower case hex digest of the gzip file) and `x-snapshot-opencode-version` (the engine that wrote it). `Content-Length` is the size of this part. `Cache-Control` is `no-store`.

WorkerResultRequest.description: The body of POST /api/workers/v1/jobs/{id}/result. The whole request body must not exceed 65536 bytes (413 otherwise). The app applies the redaction of the runner API's complete call, including the model key remembered at fetch. A result with errorCode runner_shutdown or launch_failed is not stored: the job is given back and counts an attempt.

WorkerResultResponse.description: 200 for a result and for the repetition of the same result (alreadyCompleted: true); a different result for a finished job is 409 RUNNER_RESULT_CONFLICT. After the job reached a final state only a repeat of the same result is accepted.

status.description: succeeded or failed: the job is finished. queued: the job was given back (runner_shutdown, launch_failed) and waits for another claim; it fails instead if that was the last allowed attempt. superseded (#397): the run was replaced by a newer push; its result is stored once and the job stays superseded.

WorkerErrorResponse.description: Every error of the Worker API. The same body as the runner API's ErrorResponse; the codes are those of ApiErrorCode.
